examples.japanese: {鉄骨|てっこつ}{造|づく}りのビルだ。
{工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}で{鉄骨|てっこつ}が{組|く}まれていた。
examples.english: Steel beams were being assembled at the construction site.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}は{鉄骨|てっこつ}{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート{造|づく}りで、{耐震|たいしん}{性|せい}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This building is made of steel-reinforced concrete and has high earthquake resistance.

notes:
Compound of {鉄|てつ} (iron/steel) and {骨|こつ} (bone/frame). Refers to the steel structural members used in building construction. Very common in real estate listings and construction contexts in Japan, where building structure type is a standard piece of information.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄骨|てっこつ}{造|づく}り: steel-frame construction
- {鉄骨|てっこつ}{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート{造|づく}り: steel-reinforced concrete (SRC)
- {鉄骨|てっこつ}を{組|く}む: to assemble steel frames
- {鉄骨|てっこつ}{構造|こうぞう}: steel structure

BUILDING STRUCTURE TYPES:
Japanese real estate commonly abbreviates these as:
- S{造|ぞう}: steel ({鉄骨|てっこつ})
- RC{造|ぞう}: reinforced concrete ({鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート)
- SRC{造|ぞう}: steel-reinforced concrete ({鉄骨|てっこつ}{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート)
- W{造|ぞう}: wood ({木造|もくぞう})
